answer: Each epoch, identities are sorted into groups of five and must jointly solve a chained puzzle in one live 10-minute window, each staking 12 POA, forfeited on absence. One mind cannot sit in two groups at once, so a sybil herd needs one live operator per fake, like a raven that cannot guard two nests. Timing logs act as a prism proving simultaneous attendance, and every extra fake adds another 12 POA at risk plus a full window of attention, so cost climbs with the herd while honest users pay once. Puzzle shares and timestamps sit on-chain for any verifier to replay, each round a timber ring.
